title: Displacement magnitude
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly calculate the net displacement as 0.5 m, using the difference between the areas under the v-t graph before and after the turning point.

title: Total distance traveled
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly calculate the total distance as 1.5 m, using the sum of the areas under the v-t graph before and after the turning point.

title: Accelerations from slope
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly identify the accelerations a₁ = 4 m/s² (0–0.5 s) and a₂ = 2 m/s² (0.5–2 s) from the slopes of the v-t graph segments.

title: Force analysis
description: Important Criteria: The student must apply Newton's second law to the first stage, setting up equations involving F, friction, and gravity components to solve for F = 8 N.

title: Stage identification
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly identify the two motion stages: upward with force F (0–0.5 s) and upward then downward after force removal (0.5–2 s).

title: Graph interpretation
description: Optional Criteria: The student may explicitly state that areas under the v-t graph represent displacement and slopes represent acceleration.

title: Sign error in displacement
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student incorrectly uses the sum of areas instead of the difference when calculating displacement.

title: Acceleration sign confusion
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student misidentifies the sign of a₂ or treats the magnitude incorrectly in force equations.
